note: Data for the US AI Data Center Tracker at energyriskengineering.com/data-center-tracker. Edit this file to update the live page.

projects.name: Stargate Abilene
projects.status_note: All eight buildings are topped out. Buildings 1-2 have run since late 2025, about six had been handed to OpenAI by late September 2026, and the last four are expected fully running around November 2026.
projects.power_source: 1.2 GW ERCOT interconnection with new 1 GW substation, onsite gas-turbine plant, behind-the-meter solar and batteries
projects.cooling: Closed-loop direct-to-chip liquid with air-cooled free-cooling chillers (no evaporation)
projects.water_source: Not disclosed (closed loop, zero evaporative use claimed)
projects.cost_note: $15B Crusoe/Blue Owl JV for the 1.2 GW campus. Epoch AI puts it near $31.9B including IT hardware. 1.2 GW is facility power; online MW is Epoch's IT estimate.
projects.next_milestone: Buildings 5-8 fully operational (campus complete)
projects.key_risks: A planned expansion past 1.2 GW was dropped amid financing problems and shifting OpenAI demand; Microsoft took the adjacent 900 MW. Full output depends on the onsite gas plant and new substation.

projects.name: Stargate Frontier (Shackelford)
projects.status_note: Shells for buildings 1-5 are complete and roofed, cooling and generators are going into buildings 1-3, and foundations have started on 6-7. Vantage targets first delivery in late 2026; Epoch's filing-based estimate is mid-2027.
projects.power_source: Off-grid behind-the-meter gas microgrid by VoltaGrid (Jenbacher reciprocating engines, about 700 MW first phase)
projects.utility: None (off-grid VoltaGrid microgrid in ERCOT region)
projects.cooling: Closed-loop chilled water with combined air and liquid-to-liquid cooling for 250 kW+ racks
projects.water_source: Not disclosed (Vantage claims near-zero WUE)
projects.cost_note: $25B+ Vantage campus figure. TDLR filings register $10.64B of construction; Epoch projects about $53B with IT hardware. 1,400 MW is critical IT load.
projects.next_milestone: First data center building delivered
projects.key_risks: Depends entirely on a major-source gas plant, its TCEQ air permit and gas supply; the Sept 2026 Texas pause on new TCEQ data-center permits adds uncertainty. SoftBank's pending acquisition of Vantage parent DigitalBridge.

projects.name: Stargate Milam (Freebird)
projects.status_note: The first-phase building (548,950 sq ft, four data halls) topped out in March 2026 and state filings show completion around October 2026. No capacity confirmed online yet.
projects.power_source: SB Energy-funded new generation and storage (type not disclosed) plus ERCOT grid
projects.cooling: Not disclosed
projects.water_source: Not disclosed (designed to minimize water use)
projects.cost_note: $3B is SB Energy's earlier campus plan; the phase-1 TDLR filing is about $470M. Epoch projects about $32.5B with IT. 1.2 GW is OpenAI's lease figure.
projects.next_milestone: Phase-1 building completion per TDLR filing
projects.key_risks: Power supply plan not public; execution depends on SoftBank/SB Energy financing and a new fast-build modular approach.

projects.name: Stargate Lordstown
projects.status_note: The former GM/Foxconn plant is being refit mainly as a factory for modular data-center equipment plus a smaller data-center component. Nothing operating yet; one tracker lists the data-center use as withdrawn.
projects.power_source: Grid via existing plant substation
projects.cooling: Not disclosed
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: Up to $3B for SoftBank's plant conversion, mostly manufacturing. 214 MW is Epoch's IT estimate.
projects.next_milestone: First data-center capacity operational (Epoch projection)
projects.key_risks: Unclear how much of the site will be a data center versus a factory. Village data-center permit moratorium extended in July 2026; local opposition over noise, heat and water.

projects.name: Project Jupiter (Doña Ana)
projects.developer: STACK Infrastructure (Blue Owl) and BorderPlex Digital Assets
projects.status_note: Data-center buildings were about 26% complete in September 2026. The fuel-cell microgrid awaits its state air permit and its gas pipeline has slipped to February 2027; Oracle sent a force-majeure notice while saying the schedule holds.
projects.power_source: Private onsite gas microgrid of about 2.46 GW of Bloom solid-oxide fuel cells, fed by the new Transwestern pipeline; up to 2 GW of off-site renewables sought
projects.cooling: Closed-loop non-evaporative
projects.water_source: Non-potable industrial well water (purchased farm water rights)
projects.cost_note: $165B is the developers' full-buildout estimate and county IRB authorization. 2.45 GW is campus design draw.
projects.next_milestone: NMED decision on microgrid air permit
projects.key_risks: Contested microgrid air permit, State Land Office pipeline right-of-way denial and pending FERC authorization, litigation over county bonds and incentives, and strong local opposition.

projects.name: Stargate Michigan (The Barn)
projects.status_note: All three 550,000 sq ft buildings are under construction; the first was described as nearly finished in June 2026. Completion targeted late 2027, operations early 2028.
projects.power_source: DTE grid from existing resources plus project-funded battery storage
projects.cooling: Closed-loop air-cooled system; water use said to be similar to an office building
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: $16B development and construction (up from about $7B). Totals near $43-56B are reported including Oracle's equipment fit-out. 1.4 GW is DTE's contracted supply.
projects.next_milestone: First building energized and delivered to Oracle
projects.key_risks: AG and environmental groups are appealing the MPSC's approval of the DTE contracts; local opposition after a consent judgment overrode the township's rezoning denial; possible repeal of Michigan's data-center tax break.

projects.name: Stargate Lighthouse (Port Washington)
projects.status_note: Four roughly 550,000 sq ft buildings are rising with about 3,000 workers on site, but the campus cannot run until a new ATC transmission line is approved; the PSC sent that application back in August 2026.
projects.power_source: We Energies grid via a dedicated rate: new solar, wind and battery projects plus a proposed 10-20% share of Point Beach nuclear output; diesel emergency generators
projects.cooling: Closed-loop liquid cooling
projects.water_source: Municipal (new city water main)
projects.cost_note: $15B+ Vantage campus figure, excluding the $1.3-2B+ ATC transmission project. Other sources cite a 1.3 GW grid request.
projects.next_milestone: PSC review of refiled ATC transmission application; ruling on Point Beach nuclear deal
projects.key_risks: Transmission delay: an analyst projects meaningful load no earlier than mid-to-late 2028. Lawsuit against DNR over environmental review; resident opposition over transmission costs and noise.

projects.name: Meta Hyperion
projects.status_note: Roofs are on the first two halls and the cooling plant is being installed, but nothing is energized yet. In July 2026 Meta raised the target to 5 GW and the investment to more than $50B.
projects.power_source: Entergy Louisiana grid plus 3 approved new combined-cycle gas plants (7 more requested), solar, batteries and new 500 kV transmission
projects.cooling: Air-cooled chillers (about 816 planned, per satellite imagery); liquid loop design not disclosed
projects.water_source: Not disclosed (Meta pledges 100% local watershed replenishment)
projects.cost_note: Meta's July 2026 figure of more than $50B (was $10B at groundbreaking, about $27B in the Blue Owl JV). 5,000 MW is Meta's stated compute target; Epoch counts about 1,632 MW of IT by 2028.
projects.next_milestone: First new Entergy gas units in service; PSC ruling on 7 more gas plants
projects.key_risks: Relies on regulators approving 7 more Entergy gas plants; a PSC commissioner warns of stranded costs. Scrutiny of off-balance-sheet bond financing and fast-track approvals.

projects.name: Meta Prometheus
projects.status_note: Most buildings and tent halls are running AI clusters; expansion continues while Williams finishes two behind-the-meter gas plants for the remaining halls.
projects.power_source: AEP Ohio grid (250 MW interim) plus Williams Socrates South/North behind-the-meter gas plants (400 MW) with batteries; a third plant (about 250 MW) projected for 2028
projects.utility: AEP Ohio / PJM; Williams onsite gas
projects.cooling: Direct-to-chip liquid in AI halls; air-assisted liquid racks in older halls
projects.water_source: Municipal (New Albany)
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI's projected capex for full build. Meta has disclosed only about $1.5B invested since 2017. MW figures are Epoch IT estimates; Meta's target is 1 GW by end of 2026.
projects.next_milestone: Socrates South and North gas plants fully in service
projects.key_risks: Growth depends on on-time Williams gas plants; the AEP grid feed is temporary with an 85% minimum-demand charge; onsite gas emissions draw scrutiny.

projects.name: Meta El Paso
projects.status_note: Vertical construction is under way on the 1 GW campus; a majority stake went to BlackRock in July 2026. Texas judges proposed approving the dedicated 366 MW gas plant only if ratepayers bear none of its cost.
projects.power_source: El Paso Electric grid (about 220 MW) plus a proposed 366 MW plant of modular gas generators next to the campus
projects.cooling: Closed-loop water cooling (per Meta)
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: Total development cost in the July 2026 BlackRock JV announcement (was $1.5B, then $10B+). The gas plant is a separate ~$0.5B.
projects.next_milestone: Texas PUC vote on the McCloud gas plant certificate
projects.key_risks: PUCT could deny or restrict the gas plant; the City of El Paso and over 1,000 residents oppose it. Texas's Sept 2026 pause on TCEQ data-center permits adds uncertainty.

projects.name: Meta Lebanon (LEAP District)
projects.status_note: Ground broken in February 2026 on a 1,500-acre, 13-building campus; first phase aimed at late 2027 or early 2028.
projects.power_source: Grid supply from Boone REMC / Wabash Valley Power Alliance, matched with 409 MW of new Indiana renewables
projects.cooling: Closed-loop liquid cooling that recirculates water (per Meta)
projects.water_source: Municipal (Lebanon / LEAP supply from Citizens Energy Group)
projects.cost_note: Meta's stated figure of more than $10B across up to six phases.
projects.next_milestone: First phase online
projects.key_risks: Controversy over moving regional water to the LEAP District, rate-impact concerns, and dependence on new transmission.

projects.name: xAI Colossus 1
projects.status_note: The converted Electrolux plant is fully running; since May 2026 Anthropic has leased all of its compute while xAI training moved to Colossus 2.
projects.power_source: MLGW/TVA grid (about 300 MW) plus permitted onsite gas turbines, Megapack batteries and adjacent solar
projects.cooling: Evaporative cooling towers (33 units), replacing air-cooled chillers by Feb 2026
projects.water_source: Municipal (MLGW, Memphis aquifer); planned $80M wastewater recycling plant stalled
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI's estimated capex. MW is Epoch's IT estimate.
projects.next_milestone: Construction restarts on the wastewater recycling plant
projects.key_risks: Environmental-justice opposition and air-permit disputes over the gas turbines; aquifer drawdown concerns while the recycling plant is delayed; Memphis council moratorium vote set for Oct 20.

projects.name: xAI Colossus 2
projects.status_note: Two large clusters on Tulane Road run close to 1 GW; a third building is under construction. Power comes from temporary gas turbines in Southaven, MS, to be replaced by a permitted 1.2 GW permanent plant.
projects.power_source: Mostly self-generated gas: temporary turbines in Southaven, MS, to be replaced by a 41-turbine 1.2 GW plant; Megapacks and some MLGW supply
projects.cooling: Air-cooled (dry) chillers and air-cooled condenser arrays
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI's projected capex. MW are Epoch IT estimates; Musk has claimed 2 GW eventually.
projects.next_milestone: Permanent Southaven gas plant in service; temporary turbines retired by July 2027
projects.key_risks: NAACP Clean Air Act suit, a residents' class action and an appeal of the MDEQ permit target the Southaven turbines; continuing local opposition to air pollution.

projects.name: Microsoft Fairwater (Wisconsin)
projects.status_note: Building 1 was completed and fully running by June 2026 after an April startup. Building 2 next door is under construction for 2028, and grading for a larger expansion has begun.
projects.power_source: We Energies grid; matched with carbon-free supply including 250 MW of solar; backup generators
projects.cooling: Closed-loop liquid for over 90% of the facility, outside air for the rest; air-cooled heat rejection
projects.water_source: Racine Water Utility (Lake Michigan); about 2.8M gal/yr for Phase 1
projects.cost_note: $3.3B for building 1 plus $4B for building 2 (Microsoft). Epoch estimates about $27.9B including chips. MW are Epoch IT estimates.
projects.next_milestone: Building 2 energized (Epoch projection)
projects.key_risks: Neighbor complaints about cooling-fan noise; ratepayer pushback on We Energies rate increases for about 2.6 GW of new Microsoft load.

projects.name: Microsoft Fairwater Atlanta (QTS Fayetteville)
projects.status_note: Fairwater 2 began running in October 2025 and buildings 3-4 were operating by mid-June 2026. QTS has two more shells under way on the 615-acre campus, tenant unconfirmed.
projects.power_source: Utility grid only, no onsite generation or UPS for the GPU fleet; onsite storage smooths power swings
projects.cooling: Closed-loop direct-to-chip liquid with a very large air-cooled chiller plant (about 672 units)
projects.water_source: Fayette County municipal (closed loop; small initial fill)
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI estimate including chips for buildings 1-4. Microsoft has not disclosed a cost. MW is Epoch's IT estimate.
projects.next_milestone: Fit-out of two more QTS building shells
projects.key_risks: No backup generation for the GPU halls means full utility dependence; a water-billing dispute over unmetered lines at the QTS campus; regional opposition to data-center water use.

projects.name: Microsoft Pecos
projects.status_note: Announced June 2026 with a 20-year supply deal from a co-located Chevron gas plant; capacity added over 5-7 years and no construction start published.
projects.power_source: Co-located behind-the-meter gas plant up to 2.67 GW (GE Vernova and Solar Turbines), later grid tie
projects.utility: None at launch; future ERCOT interconnection
projects.cooling: Closed-loop; initial fill only
projects.water_source: Non-potable and brackish groundwater; possible produced-water reuse
projects.cost_note: Microsoft gives only a multibillion-dollar figure.
projects.next_milestone: First power from Chevron's gas plant
projects.key_risks: Depends on Chevron building a large gas plant on schedule (turbines, air permits) amid Texas's permit pause; no grid backup at launch.

projects.name: AWS Project Rainier (New Carlisle)
projects.status_note: Phases 1-2 (18 buildings) largely run Trainium chips for Anthropic; buildings 17-18 expected around October 2026. A 14-building expansion is in site prep awaiting air and wetlands permits.
projects.power_source: I&M grid (nuclear, coal, wind) matched by about 635 MW of Amazon Indiana wind/solar; diesel backup only
projects.cooling: Mostly outside air with water-assisted cooling on hot hours; expansion adds direct-to-chip liquid
projects.water_source: New Carlisle municipal wells (shallow aquifer)
projects.cost_note: $11B AWS announced investment. Epoch estimates $72.9B at full build including chips. 2,200 MW is AWS grid draw; online MW is Epoch's IT estimate.
projects.next_milestone: Energize two new 345 kV substations (about 1.1 GW)
projects.key_risks: 345 kV substation timing, pending permits for the expansion, aquifer drawdown disputes, and a county move (Sept 22) to draft zoning barring new hyperscale campuses.

projects.name: AWS Madison County (Canton/Ridgeland)
projects.status_note: Five Canton buildings are running and buildings 6-9 have roofs on. The Ridgeland campus is in early construction after an $11-12B expansion was announced in April 2026.
projects.power_source: Entergy Mississippi grid with new Entergy gas plants and solar; 616 MW of Amazon renewable contracts; diesel backup (800+ generators)
projects.cooling: Air cooling most of the year, water about 9% of the year
projects.water_source: Canton municipal, moving to recycled wastewater in 2027; Ridgeland city water
projects.cost_note: $10B (2024) plus $11B (April 2026). MW are Epoch IT estimates for Canton only.
projects.next_milestone: Canton buildings 6-7 online; switch to recycled wastewater
projects.key_risks: Resident complaints about diesel generator noise and emissions; criticism of Entergy's confidential contract and cost recovery; water supply concerns.

projects.name: AWS Salem Twp (Susquehanna)
projects.status_note: The 1,200-acre campus has been under active construction since October 2025 around a 48 MW building Talen finished in 2023; new-building commissioning dates are TBD.
projects.power_source: Susquehanna nuclear plant (Talen) under a 1,920 MW PPA, moving to front-of-meter grid delivery
projects.cooling: Outside air most of the year, direct evaporative under 2% of the year
projects.water_source: Onsite well and Susquehanna River withdrawal plus municipal; SRBC approved
projects.cost_note: Amazon paid $650M for the campus; $20B is AWS's statewide PA pledge with no site cost. 1,920 MW is PPA volume ramping to 2032.
projects.next_milestone: Commission first Amazon-built buildings; NPDES cooling-water discharge permit
projects.key_risks: FERC earlier rejected expanding behind-the-meter supply; objections to cooling-water discharge to the Susquehanna; reactor licenses (2042/2044) cap long-term supply.

projects.name: AWS Energy Way (Richmond County)
projects.status_note: Construction on the 21-building, roughly 800-acre campus was visible by September 2026. NC DEQ issued air permits Aug 28 for Duke's temporary bridge-power engines and Amazon's backup engines; operations expected early 2027.
projects.power_source: Duke Energy Progress grid; 57 diesel bridge-power engines for about a year; 588 diesel backup engines
projects.cooling: Air cooling most of the year, water on the hottest days
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: $10B announced initial investment.
projects.next_milestone: Initial operations on Duke bridge power
projects.key_risks: Possible appeal of the air permits by SELC; organized local opposition; uncertain grid interconnection timing.

projects.name: AWS Butts County (Project Lighthouse)
projects.status_note: Early construction in River Park Industrial Park near I-75 with 12-14 buildings planned and the first targeted for 2027.
projects.power_source: Not disclosed
projects.cooling: Not disclosed
projects.water_source: Butts County Water and Sewer Authority
projects.cost_note: $11B is AWS's combined Butts and Douglas county figure. Unverified trackers cite about 786 MW.
projects.next_milestone: First building energized; PILOT payments begin
projects.key_risks: Capacity, power and water undisclosed; depends on new Georgia Power and transmission buildout and water/sewer upgrades.

projects.name: Homer City Energy Campus
projects.status_note: Vertical construction of the 4.5 GW gas plant began April 2026. AWS filed for 36 data-center buildings in phases from December 2026; the county planning commission tabled it in September.
projects.power_source: Onsite 4.4-4.5 GW gas plant (seven GE Vernova 7HA.02 turbines, Marcellus gas), over 1 GW exported to grid
projects.cooling: Not described for the data halls
projects.water_source: Former power station's existing water-withdrawal rights
projects.cost_note: $10B developer figure for campus and power plant; AWS building costs undisclosed. Planned MW is the ~3,700 MW of the 4.5 GW plant reportedly reserved for data centers.
projects.next_milestone: County decision on AWS preliminary plan; AWS phase 1 start
projects.key_risks: Air permits appealed to the Environmental Hearing Board; resident opposition (AWS plan tabled); schedule depends on turbine deliveries; very large value accumulation beside one dedicated plant.

projects.name: Google Pryor (MidAmerica Ind. Park)
projects.status_note: Running since 2011 and still growing; a converted warehouse building came online in early September 2026. The Pryor share of Google's $9B 2025 Oklahoma pledge is undisclosed.
projects.power_source: GRDA grid (Grand River Energy Center) via new on-campus substation
projects.cooling: Evaporative cooling towers (64 units, about 484 MW heat rejection)
projects.water_source: Neosho River via MidAmerica Industrial Park water system
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI estimate for the AI-compute portion (368 MW IT). Google says about $15B invested in Oklahoma since 2007.
projects.next_milestone: Pryor scope of the $9B Oklahoma investment built out
projects.key_risks: Heavy evaporative water draw (over 1.1B gallons in FY2025); new large-load cost rules under Oklahoma HB 2992.

projects.name: Google Stillwater
projects.status_note: Phase 1 lots are platted and permitted with building started on the first two. The OG&E power contract covering this campus and two Muskogee sites awaits OCC approval.
projects.power_source: OG&E grid plus two Google-backed solar farms under construction
projects.cooling: Not disclosed (about 3B gal/yr projected water use suggests water-based cooling)
projects.water_source: City of Stillwater municipal (Kaw Lake)
projects.cost_note: Earlier reported figure of up to $3B. Three OG&E-served sites (Stillwater and Muskogee) ramp to about 1 GW over 5 years with no per-site split.
projects.next_milestone: OCC ruling on OG&E-Google service agreements
projects.key_risks: Depends on OCC approval of the OG&E contract and large-load tariff; large municipal water commitment.

projects.name: Google West Memphis
projects.status_note: Ground broken October 2025 on a five-building campus with an 18-24 month build; regulators approved the supporting Entergy solar project in March 2026.
projects.power_source: Entergy Arkansas grid plus new 600 MW solar and 350 MW battery storage; onsite substation
projects.cooling: Graywater reuse plant for cooling; system type not specified
projects.water_source: Onsite graywater reuse plant
projects.cost_note: Google's announced $4B Arkansas investment through 2027.
projects.next_milestone: First building completed
projects.key_risks: Depends on Entergy's new solar and storage; pending Army Corps review of the floodplain site; 30-year PILOT deal under scrutiny.

projects.name: Project Tembo (Cheyenne)
projects.developer: Google (Jupiter Star Holdings); power by Tallgrass
projects.status_note: Crusoe exited in June 2026 and a Google subsidiary filed an amended site plan for a 2.7 GW four-hall campus. Tallgrass says its power hub is proceeding; utility service targeted early 2028.
projects.power_source: Tallgrass Cheyenne Power Hub (about 2.7 GW new gas, Mitsubishi M501JAC), plus fuel cells and Black Hills grid
projects.cooling: Not disclosed
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: No campus cost reported; about $7B is Tallgrass's power-hub investment.
projects.next_milestone: Power hub and utility service for first operations
projects.key_risks: Developer change raised cost and schedule concerns; resident objections to water use and gas emissions; long-lead turbine deliveries.

projects.name: Lake Mariner (Fluidstack/Anthropic)
projects.status_note: The first Fluidstack building began running for Anthropic around May 2026; a second is nearly finished and a third is being fitted out at this former coal-plant site on Lake Ontario.
projects.power_source: Grid (NYISO); former coal plant site
projects.cooling: Dry coolers, non-evaporative closed loop
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI projection for the Anthropic buildings. 360 MW is contracted critical IT.
projects.next_milestone: Building CB-4 energized
projects.key_risks: Third building running about a quarter late per Epoch; tied to Fluidstack financing and a Google backstop; site transmission caps expansion.

projects.name: Barber Lake (Fluidstack/Anthropic)
projects.status_note: The first building's shell, chillers and generators were mostly installed by mid-2026 but not energized. Cipher extended the lease to 20 years; first halls due late 2026 to early 2027.
projects.power_source: ERCOT grid with about 120 diesel backup generators
projects.cooling: Air-cooled chillers (about 175 units)
projects.water_source: Onsite supply (no city water)
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI projection at 207 MW critical IT (about 300 MW gross).
projects.next_milestone: First data hall delivered and rent starts
projects.key_risks: About three months behind schedule and over budget; fragile town water system, prompting a $10M repair pledge.

projects.name: Project Thunderbird (Enid)
projects.status_note: Proposed September 2026 as four campuses around Enid on about 1,750 acres; rezoning filed for two sites, with no city water agreement and no tenant yet.
projects.power_source: Behind-the-meter gas plant up to 3.3 GW; not grid-supplied
projects.cooling: Closed-loop recirculating
projects.water_source: Raw water from Kaw Lake pipeline (agreement pending)
projects.cost_note: Developer's estimate of up to $35B. 2.75 GW is IT load.
projects.next_milestone: Rezoning hearings (planning commission and city commission)
projects.key_risks: Needs zoning, a water deal, a tenant, financing and air permits for a 3.3 GW gas plant; organized local opposition.

projects.name: IREN Project Emerald (Kiowa)
projects.status_note: IREN owns part of the roughly 2,000-acre site and a county committee endorsed the tax-incentive plan; commissioners have not voted on the TIF districts and a public-vote petition is being prepared.
projects.power_source: PSO grid interconnection (studies complete)
projects.cooling: Closed-loop recirculating (per IREN)
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: About $50B across two phases per county documents; capacity figures conflict (1.6 GW vs 1.2 GW per phase).
projects.next_milestone: County commissioners vote on TIF districts
projects.key_risks: TIF not approved and abatement may face a public vote; uncertain local water; no signed tenant.

projects.name: Fermi Project Matador (Amarillo)
projects.tenant: TensorWave (first lease, 222 MW, options to 650 MW)
projects.status_note: Site and power-plant groundwork is under way for six Siemens SGT-800 turbines. A first lease with TensorWave was signed in August 2026 but closing depends on financing; nothing in service yet.
projects.power_source: Private onsite grid: gas turbines plus a proposed 2.6 GW gas plant, four planned AP1000 nuclear units, solar and batteries
projects.cooling: Not specified (company claims about 80% less water than conventional)
projects.water_source: City of Amarillo (up to 2.5 MGD) plus Ogallala-region groundwater leases
projects.cost_note: Midpoint of a reported $70-90B+ estimate. Planned MW is the stated up-to-11 GW project; generation plans have grown to about 17 GW.
projects.next_milestone: TensorWave lease closing and project financing
projects.key_risks: No revenue and dependent on new capital; CEO firing litigation and a securities class action; air-permit challenges; Ogallala water scrutiny; unlicensed nuclear plans.

projects.name: Applied Digital Polaris Forge 1
projects.status_note: Two buildings are live with 250 MW of critical IT (building 2's second phase on Oct 1, 2026); a third 150 MW building is under construction.
projects.power_source: Regional grid (excess transmission capacity)
projects.cooling: Closed-loop (company general description)
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: No total cost reported; $1.59B of notes fund the third building. MW are critical IT.
projects.next_milestone: Third 150 MW building ready for service
projects.key_risks: Heavy debt load and single-tenant dependence on CoreWeave; note amortization tied to lease start makes delays costly.

projects.name: CoreWeave Lancaster
projects.developer: Chirisa / Machine Investment Group (JV with Blue Owl)
projects.status_note: Phase one converts a former printing plant; July 2026 imagery showed rooftop cooling going in but not yet running. Phase two needs city planning approval.
projects.power_source: PPL grid via new substation and switchyard; backup generators
projects.cooling: Rooftop air-cooled chillers
projects.water_source: Not disclosed (SRBC caps about 20,000 gal/day per site)
projects.cost_note: $6B CoreWeave commitment; 100 MW initial scalable to 300 MW.
projects.next_milestone: Building 1 operational (about 92 MW IT)
projects.key_risks: City zoning appeals, phase-two approval, and PPL substation timing.

projects.name: Prince William Digital Gateway
projects.status_note: Dead: courts voided the rezoning (affirmed March 2026) and QTS withdrew its last appeal on July 2, 2026.
projects.power_source: Not disclosed
projects.cooling: Not disclosed
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: QTS had claimed tens of billions for about 23M sq ft.
projects.next_milestone: None
projects.key_risks: Any revival needs new rezoning against strong battlefield-preservation opposition; county cut its by-right data-center district by two-thirds on Sept 25.

news.headline: Cipher doubled lease terms at its 300 MW Colorado City campus to 20 years, lifting contracted revenue above $9B; halls now due Q4 2026 to Q1 2027.
news.why_it_matters: Long leases support project debt, but shifted handover dates and overrun-sharing terms signal schedule pressure during commissioning.

news.headline: A $366M first building, reportedly tied to Anthropic, was filed near Austin with up to 710 MW of simple-cycle gas turbines planned on site.
news.why_it_matters: Behind-the-meter simple-cycle fleets put turbine breakdown, fuel supply and fire exposures together on one site.

news.headline: Raleigh's council voted 7-1 to pause approvals of large data centers for six months while it drafts new rules.
news.why_it_matters: More local pauses across the Southeast add permitting and schedule risk to projects still in planning.

news.headline: The Memphis council's data-center moratorium vote collapsed into protests and a fight and was pushed to October 20.
news.why_it_matters: The outcome could restrict further builds near the Colossus sites.

news.headline: Google signed for 3.6 GW from Constellation, including a 20-year 890 MW nuclear PPA tied to $4.3B of upgrades at 11 reactors.
news.why_it_matters: Uprate and life-extension work at operating nuclear units adds construction and operational exposure to nuclear and power books.

news.headline: AWS filed plans for 36 two-story buildings on 1,100 acres at Homer City, powered mainly by the 4.5 GW gas plant under construction next door.
news.why_it_matters: A very large value accumulation beside one dedicated plant makes power-loss business interruption the central question.

news.headline: TeraWulf doubled its Kentucky Power service agreement to 1 GW and pulled the second 500 MW phase forward to 2029.
news.why_it_matters: Delivery hinges on a new 765/345 kV substation and regulator approval: a single-point grid dependency.

news.headline: Applied Digital finished Building 2 at its CoreWeave-leased Ellendale campus, bringing live IT load to 250 MW of a planned 400 MW.
news.why_it_matters: Phased energization puts live halls beside active construction, mixing hot work and commissioning with operating exposure.

news.headline: Crusoe filed two satellite buildings worth $4.8B in Kent County, taking its Childress-linked Project Hyper to about $12B.
news.why_it_matters: Remote West Texas sites with limited fire service and severe convective storm exposure, carrying multibillion-dollar builder's risk values.

news.headline: We Energies reached a deal to supply the Oracle campus in Port Washington partly with output from Point Beach nuclear plant.
news.why_it_matters: Adds a firm supply leg, but the campus still cannot run until its new transmission line is approved.

news.headline: Governor Spanberger's executive order bans project NDAs and orders reviews of diesel backup generator impacts and new noise rules.
news.why_it_matters: Tighter diesel limits could change emergency power design and fuel storage in the largest US market.

news.headline: A 57-43 Senate vote fell short of cloture on a House-passed bill making data centers pay full grid-upgrade costs.
news.why_it_matters: Cost allocation stays a state-by-state patchwork, so tariff and collateral terms vary by site.

news.headline: Amazon signed a 20-year deal for 690 MW from Calvert Cliffs nuclear plant, backing more than $3B of upgrades and about 190 MW of new output.
news.why_it_matters: Hyperscaler-funded nuclear uprates bring large outage-and-upgrade construction exposure to operating plants.

news.headline: Valar Atomics applied to BLM for a Carbon County campus of about 456 small reactors, up to 9.6 GW, with fuel and waste facilities.
news.why_it_matters: Would co-locate unproven Gen IV reactors with data halls at a scale no nuclear pool has written.

news.headline: A weak tornado touched down among wind turbines about four miles from a Google data-center build in the Panhandle, causing no damage.
news.why_it_matters: A near miss that shows Panhandle campuses' tornado exposure.

news.headline: FERC suspended PJM's 6.8 GW emergency backstop capacity auction until February 2027, citing cost-allocation and collateral flaws.
news.why_it_matters: PJM's capacity shortfall persists, raising curtailment risk for Mid-Atlantic data centers.

news.headline: Prince William supervisors cut the county's by-right data-center district by about two-thirds, to 3,500 acres.
news.why_it_matters: Sites outside the smaller zone now face full review, slowing Northern Virginia pipelines.

news.headline: Applied Digital sited its $3.2B, 210 MW hyperscaler campus on 1,300 acres near Brookwood in Tuscaloosa County, opening 2028.
news.why_it_matters: A new multibillion-dollar build in a county with significant wind and convective storm exposure.

news.headline: Oracle sent Blue Owl a force-majeure notice after the gas pipeline for the 2.45 GW campus slipped to February 2027.
news.why_it_matters: Fuel-supply delays for onsite fuel-cell power are triggering contract relief: a clear delay-in-start-up warning.

news.headline: DOE picked 31 reconductoring and grid-upgrade projects for $1.9B, aiming to free about 23 GW of transfer capacity for large loads.
news.why_it_matters: Transmission helps interconnection but adds no generation, so onsite power stays the norm.

news.headline: Reporting shows El Paso Electric considered only gas to power Meta's campus, as a ruling on the dedicated 366 MW plant nears.
news.why_it_matters: A PUC denial or restriction would leave the 1 GW campus short of firm power.

news.headline: Governor Abbott froze new state environmental permits for data centers until ERCOT finishes its large-load audit, expected in December.
news.why_it_matters: Air permits for onsite turbines are on hold, putting a large share of the Texas pipeline at risk of delay.

news.headline: Newsom signed seven bills creating rate classes for 25 MW+ loads, requiring sworn water-use reporting and ending blanket CEQA exemptions.
news.why_it_matters: Water and energy disclosure will shape cooling choices and permit timelines in California.

news.headline: The county council voted 6-3 to start drafting zoning that would bar new hyperscale campuses; a final vote is expected within 60 days.
news.why_it_matters: The county hosts about 40 Amazon and Microsoft buildings, so future expansions face headwinds.

news.headline: New Era signed a 20-year PPA with Vistra's Luminant for at least 207 MW from the adjacent 1.1 GW Odessa gas plant.
news.why_it_matters: Supply from one neighboring plant concentrates outage risk; contingent business interruption needs review.

news.headline: Residents and an environmental group sued to void tax abatements and a land sale for a 3.2 GW OpenAI-linked campus, alleging secret dealings.
news.why_it_matters: A successful open-meetings challenge could unwind incentives and delay a coastal Georgia gigawatt build.

news.headline: Salem adopted an extendable 120-day data-center moratorium, halting phase one of Verrus's $5.1B campus.
news.why_it_matters: Shows local action can strand construction schedules and financing mid-stream.
